Card as shown:
Front: Production possibilities frontier (PPF)
Question: What does a production possibilities frontier show, and what is held constant?
Answer: The maximum combinations of two goods an economy can produce when it uses all its resources efficiently, with resources and technology held fixed. It is a snapshot at one point in time.
Example: Boots and jackets: 0 boots and 100 jackets, 20 and 90, 40 and 70, 60 and 40, or 80 and 0.
Watch out: Prices don't appear anywhere on a PPF.
note: Is this correct? Doesn't a PPF show the maximum combination of two or more goods an economy can produce...? Through our learned example we use two goods to simplify but in reality it is more.
reply: You're right that real economies make many goods. The PPF uses two only so it fits on a graph. The card now says so.
